newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. energy authority wants $125 mln bond sale.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. energy authority wants $125 mln bond sale.

text.p: The New York State Energy Research and Development Authority said on Wednesday it wants to sell more than $125 million of bonds in two separate offerings, but the sale still must be approved by Albany.
An up to $101.9 million sale of variable-rate refunding bonds was anticipated for August, along with as much as $25.5 million of bonds to be sold in a forward refunding.

The projects originally paid for facilities to treat water pollution at two Rochester plants owned by Rochester Gas and Electric Corp, as well as equipment to treat air and water pollution and solid waste at a Nine Mile Point Nuclear Station Unit in Scriba, New York. The company has a 14 percent stake in the plant.
Both offerings would be backed by an irrevocable promissory note issued by the utility and by bond insurance to be obtained from MBIA Insurance Corp.
The utility estimated that the tax-exempt financings would produce about $93.7 million in interest cost savings over the life of the bonds.
A spokesman for the energy authority said the state board that must approve debt sales, the Public Authorities Control Board, next was expected to meet on July 16.
